decisions.decision: Old phase folders were intentionally discarded.
decisions.rationale: The user deleted them because they were too noisy; recreated folders do not inherit stale verification.

decisions.decision: Phase01A storage foundation lands before Hub wiring.
decisions.rationale: Migration and repository contract can be verified independently before touching channel/chat runtime behavior.

decisions.decision: Run execution facts use SQLite `runs` snapshots plus append-only `run_events`.
decisions.rationale: This follows ADR-019 and preserves cache/logs as non-canonical support planes.

decisions.decision: The Hub lifecycle store seam is optional and stores metadata-level lifecycle events only.
decisions.rationale: This keeps existing adapter delivery behavior stable while preventing raw prompts, channel data, and raw loop errors from becoming default stored event payloads.

decisions.decision: Hub persists tool/usage/final-output metadata with an allowlist.
decisions.rationale: PRD Phase 1A requires durable tool names, call ids, argument keys, status, timing, usage, and final output without raw argument values or raw tool result payloads by default.

decisions.decision: Phase01B first slice is schema plus `internal/identity`, not direct channel rewiring.
decisions.rationale: The source audit found auth, Telegram, cron, swarm, and tool allowlists all depend on the same missing authority boundary; landing schema/default-deny Authorize first prevents broad cross-surface churn.
Migration/identity tests, targeted build/vet, repo-wide build/vet, and full Go tests pass.

decisions.rationale: Subagent goal verifier returned PASS 10/10 for Phase01B1 only, and code-risk recheck returned PASS 9.5/10 with no B1 blockers. Phase01B2 is now locally implemented, while dashboard/API/tool/cron/swarm/denial-event wiring remains planned B3-B7 work.

decisions.decision: Phase01B2 backfills persisted Telegram allowlist identity without removing `allowed_users`.
decisions.rationale: Migration v8 backfills real persisted `allowed_users` rows into deterministic Telegram principals, channel accounts, session actors, and grants; auth bootstrap/approval creates the same rows for newly allowed users. E2E bootstrap rows remain excluded from real-user identity backfill.
